column1: # Fixup order for tools/fixorder.py: object stem, then every fixup of the object as a data
# offset (hex, from the start of its code segment), in the order TLINK must see them.
# HPSHRINK (src/heap/HPSHRINK.C, image 0x1676..0x1754). CPP.EXE's relocation table lists
# entries #33-#36 as 16A5h (SHRINK_HEAP_FULLY's far call to SHRINK_HEAP_TO, the segment
# word of offset 2Dh), 167Bh, 169Ah and 16B3h (the DGROUP loads at 5h, 24h and 3Dh).
# Turbo C 2.01 -B, which gives every byte of the file, writes them through TASM 2.51 as
# 5h, 24h, 3Dh, 2Dh. Evidence for moving the far call to the front, and nothing else:
#  - TASM 2.51 only puts a far call before such DGROUP/seg fixups when the call's target
#    is already declared at the call (tested with small TASM modules: only a target declared before the call moves it). Here the
#    target is a later function of the same file, and Turbo C writes its extrns at the
#    end of its -B output, so no source we can write gives the order. Split files cannot
#    give it either: TLINK keeps object order, and GATHER_ALL_FREE_SPACE's load (167Bh)
#  - BC 2.0 and Turbo C 2.01 compiled directly give fully descending order; TASM 1.0, 2.0
#    and 2.51, TLINK 3.0 and 4.0, and Turbo C++ 1.01 were also tried (docs/FINDINGS.md).
#  - BCC.EXE has the same relocation order for the same functions, so it is how the
#    original was built, not a slip in CPP.EXE alone.
# The other fixups keep TASM's order; loc-1 (offset) fixups make no relocation entries.
